discovery: Discovery and theory of excitonic Bose-Einstein condensation (spontaneous interlayer coherence) in quantum Hall bilayers

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (mesoscopic and low-dimensional electron systems)
motivation: In closely spaced two-dimensional electron bilayers at total filling factor one, electrons in one layer bind to holes in the other, forming a Bose-Einstein condensate of excitons with spontaneous interlayer phase coherence. Girvin and MacDonald, with collaborators, predicted this broken-symmetry state, its pseudospin ferromagnetism, Goldstone mode and counterflow superfluidity. Eisenstein's group, through exceptionally clean double-quantum-well samples and meticulous independent-contact measurements, observed the giant Josephson-like zero-bias tunneling peak, vanishing counterflow Hall and longitudinal resistance, perfect Coulomb drag, and Corbino-geometry exciton transport. Together these established the first unambiguous solid-state exciton condensate, a macroscopic quantum state born purely of Coulomb interactions. The work defined a field that now extends to graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide bilayers, and remains a model of how careful heterostructure engineering and measurement integrity can reveal deep many-body physics.
